description: Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.

a.request: Looking only at films that have at least one copy in inventory (films with no copies are left out completely, including from every average), count each film's inventory copies. For each film, show its id, its rating, its number of copies, its copy count minus the average copy count per film for films of the same rating, and its copy count minus the overall average copy count per film (averaged over the individual films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the difference from the overall average, largest first, and keep the top 10 (ties broken arbitrarily). Do not round.
a.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copy_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating) SELECT film_id, rating, copy_count, copy_count - AVG(copy_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS rating_avg_difference, copy_count - AVG(copy_count) OVER () AS overall_avg_difference FROM film_copies ORDER BY overall_avg_difference DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Return the 10 films with the largest number of inventory copies above the overall average copies per stocked film, sorted by that difference descending; for each, show its film ID, rating, copy count, difference from the average for stocked films with the same rating, and difference from the overall average across all stocked films, with no rounding and ties in any order
b.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copy_count FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), comparisons AS (SELECT film_id, rating, copy_count, copy_count - AVG(copy_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS difference_from_rating_average, copy_count - AVG(copy_count) OVER () AS difference_from_overall_average FROM film_copies) SELECT film_id, rating, copy_count, difference_from_rating_average, difference_from_overall_average FROM comparisons WHERE difference_from_overall_average > 0 ORDER BY difference_from_overall_average DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Which 10 films have the most inventory copies compared with the average number of copies per film? For each, show the film id, its rating, its number of copies, how far that is from the average copies per film for its rating, and how far it is from the overall average copies per film (averaged over films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the overall difference, largest first. Ties can go in any order, and nothing is rounded. Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.
c.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT i.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory AS i JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY i.film_id, f.rating), copy_averages AS (SELECT film_id, rating, copies, AVG(copies) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS rating_avg, AVG(copies) OVER () AS overall_avg FROM film_copies) SELECT film_id, rating, copies, copies - rating_avg AS rating_difference, copies - overall_avg AS overall_difference FROM copy_averages ORDER BY overall_difference DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Which 10 films have the most inventory copies above the overall average copies per film? For each, show the film ID, rating, number of copies, difference from the average for its rating, and difference from the overall average. Compute both averages using only films with at least one inventory copy, ignoring missing values. Sort by the overall difference, largest first; ties may appear in any order. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT i.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory AS i JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY i.film_id, f.rating), averages AS (SELECT film_id, rating, copies, AVG(copies) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS rating_avg, AVG(copies) OVER () AS overall_avg FROM film_copies) SELECT film_id, rating, copies, copies - rating_avg AS difference_from_rating_average, copies - overall_avg AS difference_from_overall_average FROM averages WHERE copies > overall_avg ORDER BY difference_from_overall_average DESC LIMIT 10;
